title: Recreation league court slots
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

A recreational badminton club can rent only two of its three weekly court slots next season. Fictional historical data for the last five weeks give attendance and total waitlist counts by slot. Tuesday attendance was 10, 11, 12, 10, 12 with waitlists 0, 1, 3, 0, 2. Thursday attendance was 8, 9, 8, 11, 9 with waitlists 0, 0, 0, 1, 0. Sunday attendance was 12, 12, 11, 12, 12 with waitlists 4, 5, 1, 4, 3. Each slot holds 12 players and weekly rents are $44, $36, and $62 respectively. Compare all pairs under a $110 weekly cap using attendance, unmet demand, and cost per visit. Choose offline deliverables and start from an empty directory.

BOOKING RECOMMENDATION

Keep Tuesday and Sunday.

At $106 per week, this pair fits the $110 cap with $4 to spare. It served 114 of 120 available visits over five weeks, the highest attendance of any pair. Choose it if the club’s priority is serving the most players at their historically requested times.

What the rent buys

All three pairs fit the weekly cap. Visit and demand counts below cover the full five weeks.

Tuesday + Thursday offers the lowest cost per visit. Keeping Sunday instead of Thursday costs $26 more per week and serves 14 more visits over five weeks. Thursday + Sunday saves $8 per week versus the recommendation, but serves 10 fewer visits and costs more per visit.

How to read unmet demand. The records contain 183 slot requests (159 visits plus 24 waitlist entries). Assuming nobody shifts to another day, total unmet equals retained waitlists plus all requests for the dropped slot. For Tuesday + Sunday, that is 23 waitlist entries plus 46 Thursday requests, or 69 unmet. These counts measure requests, not unique people. Cost per visit divides five weeks of rent by visits served.
